chapter: Recent years and early piano influences
title: Band piano solos and the microphone
summary: Band pianists played solos while the drummer rested; microphones later allowed Basie's economy.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Well, he always said he was a band pianist.

Very few could play like that. Usually in the old days, when a piano solo occurred in an arrangement for a big band, the drummer would take a rest and the piano would play alone. I saw Fletcher do that at the Savoy, Fletcher Henderson. The drummer would just fold his arms, and it was beautiful. People could hardly hear. They noticed they were playing, you know. There was no amplification, however -- nothing. And then, when he finished his solo, the band resumed playing.

See, with the advent of microphone becoming popular later on, they put the microphone on the piano, and the lowest single notes or anything like that... You could hear everything. Therefore, that's where Mister Count Basie eventually...where he had to really play... All he had to do was play his right hand and let the rhythm section go, yet you could hear the tinkle on the right hand! Although, you know, he was a good player. He could play the full keyboard, you know. But he became effective at what he did.
Then prior to that, too, was Teddy Wilson. Now, Teddy Wilson...
Well, let's not get too far along.
